action_summary: Wave 45 replaced a degenerate learned pattern with a transferable rule and claimed only that the rule fires on a renamed instance. This wave asks the question that claim makes askable, on real histories rather than fixtures: harvest 400 commits each from python-attrs/attrs and pallets/click into 1,600 single-statement repairs, learn rules from one side, and see whether any rule reproduces a repair it never saw. It does not: 4 of 163 within a project (2.45%) against 5 of 163 for verbatim traces (3.07%), and 0 of 1,350 across projects, although 76.4% of the held-out repairs share a root shape with some stored rule. The abstraction does not beat transcription, so retrieval on the shape of an edit is not the bottleneck -- the trigger is.

load_bearing_primary.interpretation: OSWorld 2.0's authors diagnose frontier failure as weak recovery and maintenance of hidden state. A computer-use agent's action is only as good as the invocation it can compose from what the environment declares. Round 7 measured that the composition was wrong for reasons the environment had already published: the same 20 programs yield 33 doors when their declarations are misread and 57 when they are read, with no new knowledge acquired. No benchmark task was run; no discharge is claimed.
